result.summary: Sets `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` instead of `SO_REUSEADDR` on P2P listen sockets when running on Windows. Also adds a functional test verifying that another socket cannot bind to the active P2P listen port.
result.problem: On Windows, `SO_REUSEADDR` semantics allow another process running under the same user account to bind to a port already in use by `bitcoind`. This allows malicious or accidental local processes to intercept incoming P2P network traffic.
evidence: PR description citing Microsoft Winsock documentation: 'on Windows, SO_REUSEADDR does not carry over the same semantics as on POSIX systems. a second socket can set SO_REUSEADDR and bind to a port that is already in use by another process running under the same user account.'
Precedent in merged PR #36169, which applied the same `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` fix to HTTP/RPC listen sockets on Windows.

result.card: Sets SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE instead of SO_REUSEADDR on P2P listen sockets on Windows, accompanied by a test to verify port exclusivity. On Windows, default SO_REUSEADDR semantics permit another process under the same user account to bind to an occupied port and intercept incoming P2P connections. This extends the socket exclusivity behavior previously merged for RPC listeners in PR #36169.

risk.why: Incorrect socket option handling or edge cases on Windows could cause bitcoind to fail to bind its P2P listening port on startup or restart.
